outcome: Planned deliveries (induced or elective cesarean sections)
Nonlabor cesarean sections indications (hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, breech presentation, fetal distress, previous cesarean sections)
cohort: The study included 2,946,851 babies born to 1,627,408 mothers in Australia and New Zealand, comparing 211 deliveries from 137 mothers with a functioning kidney transplant to those without kidney replacement therapy.
finding: Women with a kidney transplant have significantly higher rates of cesarean section delivery, even after adjusting for maternal factors, preterm delivery, and past cesarean sections.
mod_finding: Mothers with a kidney transplant experienced higher rates of cesarean sections (63% vs 26%), less spontaneous labor (30% vs 63%), and more planned deliveries (70% vs 36%), with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy and breech presentation being primary drivers for planned cesareans.
